deep.reconstruction:
The main content of folio 37r is not mathematics. It is a French draft of a cover letter, almost certainly addressed to the (perpetual) Secretary of the Académie des Sciences in Paris.

My reading of the text: "Monsieur, J'ai eu l'honneur de vous soumettre, il y a quelques jours, sous l'adresse du Secrétariat de l'Institut, un mémoire relatif à une question proposée par l'Académie comme sujet de prix et portant l'épigraphe : Et his principiis via sternitur ad majora. Je vous prie, monsieur, de l'admettre au concours, si cela est possible. Je pense qu'on y trouvera la question résolue ; mais faute de temps, je n'ai pas pu exposer tous les calculs en détail, de sorte que ce mémoire en tout cas aurait besoin d'une nouvelle ré[daction] …" The draft breaks off at 'ré'.

The epigraph identifies the memoir. It is Riemann's Paris prize essay on the conduction of heat in homogeneous anisotropic bodies, the 'Commentatio mathematica, qua respondere tentatur quaestioni ab Ill.ma Academia Parisiensi propositae'. It was submitted in 1861 under this motto and printed posthumously in the Gesammelte Werke (1876).

The draft adds three biographical details:
- Riemann sent the memoir a few days earlier, addressed generally to the Secretariat of the Institut.
- He asks that it be admitted to the competition 'if possible', which suggests it arrived at or after the deadline, or through irregular channels.
- He concedes that, for lack of time, the calculations are not fully worked out and the memoir would need re-editing.

The last point matches the historical outcome. The prize was not awarded to Riemann, in part because the proofs were judged insufficiently developed.

Mathematical scraps (faint pencil, upside down or bled through at the top of the sheet, mostly illegible):
- A sum of six variables, x+y+z+t+u+v.
- Expressions of the form y(y-1)=…, …(1-y) and 1+1/y.
- Small rows of '+' signs.
- Near the lower right, two small columns of three-digit strings (roughly 133/113/111 and 113/113/133).

These match the facing pages. The next page imposes x+y+z+t+u+v=0 together with px+qy+rz+p't+q'u+r'v=0. Both the next page and the previous page work with tables of binary theta characteristics written as triples like 100, 101, 111. That is, the scraps belong to Riemann's study of relations among genus-3 theta characteristics: the 28 odd, 36 even and Göpel-type systems indicated by the counts 28·27·16/6 and 36·35·16/6 on the previous page.

No derivation on this page is legible enough to reconstruct, so I attempt none beyond this identification.
errors: No mathematical errors can be assessed; the calculations are too faint to read.
The letter draft is incomplete; it breaks off at 'ré[daction]'.

results.what: Draft cover letter asking the Paris Académie to admit to the prize competition a memoir with the epigraph 'Et his principiis via sternitur ad majora', with an admission that the calculations are not fully detailed.
results.modern_name: Riemann's 1861 Paris prize memoir on heat conduction in anisotropic bodies (Commentatio mathematica), containing the curvature criterion for flatness of a quadratic differential form.

results.what: Faint scraps of calculations with six variables x,y,z,t,u,v and binary characteristic triples.
results.modern_name: Combinatorics of genus-3 theta characteristics (odd/even characteristics, Göpel systems); context from adjacent pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The memoir, its epigraph, its late submission and the judgment that its proofs were insufficient are all well documented. A French draft of the cover letter is a minor archival and biographical detail; it confirms Riemann's own awareness that the memoir needed re-editing. The marginal mathematics is illegible scrap from his theta-characteristic work.

checkable.asserts: Genus 3 has 36 even and 28 odd theta characteristics, the counts used on the adjacent pages (context only; not legible on this page).
Arithmetic of the count 28·27·16/(1·2·3) appearing on the previous page (context).

transcription_corrections: The letter ends 'aurait besoin d'une nouvelle ré…', almost certainly to be completed as 'rédaction'.
'de l'admettre au concours, si cela est possible' is the correct reading; the image shows a correction or blot around 'de l'admettre'.
'Secrétariat de l'Institut' is confirmed in the image.
The folio number '37' is written in the right margin.

The top-of-page formulas are extremely faint and probably bleed-through or inverted. Only x+y+z+t+u+v and fragments like y(y-1), (1-y), 1+1/y are plausible; the rest of the machine guesses should be treated as unreliable.

Bottom right has two small columns of three-digit strings, roughly 133/113/111 and 113/113/133 (uncertain). These are not in the machine transcription and are probably theta-characteristic labels like those on the next page.
